solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Advance cast picked up after rest

indicators.note: after places the spoken piece behind the word for rest

parts.note: a rest is a break, a pause in work

indicators.note: picked up as by a listener's ear, so the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: to cast is to throw; its past tense is threw

explanation.surface: An actor's cast collects a big step forward once they've had their break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' signals a sound-alike; 'after' sets the heard word behind the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A significant advance or discovery is a breakthrough; synonym in the sense of progress.

clue.text: So what beings periodically give people a hand?

indicators.note: periodically means at intervals, so every other letter of the word is used

parts.note: to deal is to give out cards, so each player gets a hand

explanation.surface: Should we care whether creatures now and then lend people some help?
explanation.walkthrough: 'a hand' is a hand of cards, not help.
explanation.definitionFit: Big deal is a dismissive idiom meaning it hardly matters, much as 'so what' does.

clue.text: Writer, say, English are inclined to defend say

indicators.note: to defend is to guard by surrounding, so the leaning word encloses the example

parts.note: to list is to lean or tilt, like a ship
eg (for example) means say

explanation.surface: An author claims the English tend to protect free speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' appears twice: once in the definition, once as the example abbreviation wrapped by 'to defend'.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegist writes elegies, mournful poems, so is one example of a writer.

clue.text: Royal wrapping the present on purpose

indicators.note: wrapping means enclosing, so the royal word goes round the other piece

parts.note: kingly means royal
the present moment is now

explanation.surface: A monarch deliberately wraps a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift; it is the present time.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something knowingly is doing it deliberately, intentionally.

clue.text: Cries of surprise rising in commotion

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means reading upwards, so the cries are reversed

parts.note: ah and ooh are both cries of surprise

explanation.surface: Gasps go up amid a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses AH OOH.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoo-ha is a fuss or uproar, informal for commotion.

clue.text: Something in the air helping speech

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen, found in air
a ration is a portion, a helping

explanation.surface: An atmosphere-related matter assists a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something in the air' suggests a feeling, but it is oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal speech, given on a ceremonial occasion.

clue.text: Sneer, maybe, from British king, a symbol of authority

parts.note: GRI stands for Georgius Rex Imperator, King George as King and Emperor
a mace is a ceremonial staff, a symbol of authority

explanation.surface: A sneer, perhaps, from a British monarch bearing his ceremonial staff.
explanation.walkthrough: GRI, Latin for George, King and Emperor, appeared on British royal insignia.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneer is one kind of grimace, a twisted facial expression; hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Merge foolishly with Etonian group of egoists

indicators.note: foolishly means senselessly, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A silly merger with an Old Etonian among a self-obsessed set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolishly' rearranges MERGE ETONIAN. An Etonian attended Eton, the English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: The Me Generation was the label for 1970s baby boomers seen as self-absorbed.

clue.text: Drawer retiring greengrocer gleefully stocks

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing, read here as going backwards
the phrase stocks the letters, holding them inside its words

explanation.surface: A retired greengrocer happily keeps some goods in stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocks' signals the letters OCERGLE inside greengrocer gleefully; 'retiring' reverses them. 'Drawer' is one who draws: a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: El Greco was a Spanish Renaissance painter, and an artist who draws is a drawer.

clue.text: There's no change at all in these organs

parts.note: no, as nothing or zero, is the letter O
to change is to vary; with 'There's' it reads as varies

explanation.surface: Someone insists nothing at all changes in certain body parts.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the opening as 'nil varies': O for no, then VARIES for change.
explanation.definitionFit: The ovaries are the female reproductive organs that produce eggs.

clue.text: Creep hard to put in jail is a big hitter

indicators.note: to put in places these pieces inside the word for jail

parts.note: the slammer is slang for jail
to edge is to creep forward
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A villain sent down for being a hard-hitting thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creep' looks like a nasty person; it means to inch forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A sledgehammer is a heavy long-handled hammer, a tool for hitting very hard.

clue.text: Corps in retreat — I note they served with honour

indicators.note: in retreat means going backwards, so the corps abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
ti (te) is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A military unit falls back while someone remarks on those who served honourably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' reverses REME to EMER.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeriti are those retired from office, such as professors, who keep their title as an honour.

clue.text: Disturb the thing set in stone

indicators.note: set in, like a gem in a mount, puts one piece inside another

parts.note: agate is a semi-precious stone
it is a pronoun standing for the thing

explanation.surface: Don't disturb something that is carved in stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set in stone' reads as a fixed phrase; here 'set in' is the instruction, as a gem is set in a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to stir up or trouble, a synonym for disturb.

clue.text: One in account knocked back port

indicators.note: knocked back means sent backwards, so the whole is reversed
in places the numeral inside the story

parts.note: a tale is an account or story
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: One person's account of a harbour is rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives TALIE; 'knocked back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eilat is Israel's port on the Red Sea, at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba.

clue.text: Beg urgent reforms for pioneering pressman?

indicators.note: reforms means forms again, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plea for urgent change from a trailblazing journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' rearranges BEG URGENT. 'pressman' points to a printing press, not journalism.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Gutenberg introduced movable-type printing in Europe, a pioneer of the printing press.

clue.text: What child may want: spin around Britain's capital in hurry

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the word for hurry

parts.note: to tear is to rush, hurry
to eddy is to spin around, as water does in a whirlpool

indicators.note: a word's capital is its initial letter

explanation.surface: A child rushes round Britain's capital in a whirl, wanting something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like London; it is the first letter of Britain's.
explanation.definitionFit: A teddy bear is the cuddly toy that a young child would ask for.

clue.text: Fought about indeed turning hawk-like

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for fought goes round the other piece

parts.note: to fight verbally is to argue

indicators.note: turning means turned round, so the word is reversed

parts.note: yes is an emphatic indeed

explanation.surface: A combatant who quarrelled grows sharp-eyed and predatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' and 'about' are the two instructions. Argus was the many-eyed watchman of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Argus-eyed means keenly watchful, as sharp-sighted as a hawk.

clue.text: Greet us waving, perhaps?

indicators.note: waving means moving to and fro, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone greeting us with a wave makes a movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waving' rearranges GREET US, and the whole clue then describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Waving to greet someone is an example of a gesture, a movement conveying meaning.

clue.text: Big cheese and more crackers after drink

indicators.note: after puts the scrambled letters behind the drinking word

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Eating more cheese and biscuits following a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big cheese' and 'crackers' build a food scene; crackers means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is the person in overall charge, like a big cheese or top boss.

clue.text: Hit band pocketing millions

indicators.note: pocketing means putting away inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a sash is a band of cloth worn round the body
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A chart-topping group rakes in a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit band' looks like a successful pop group; 'Hit' is the definition, a sash the band.
explanation.definitionFit: A smash is a great success, a sell-out hit.

clue.text: Old Arab people hospitalised?

indicators.note: the question mark flags that being hospitalised means being put inside a medical institution, so the people go within it

parts.note: a san is short for sanatorium, where someone hospitalised might be
a race is a people

explanation.surface: An elderly Arab is admitted to hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hospitalised' does double duty: it supplies the sanatorium and signals putting the people inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Saracen was the medieval European name for an Arab or Muslim, especially in the Crusades.

clue.text: Sculpture made in great institutions of learning

indicators.note: in places the reshaped letters inside the word for great

parts.note: ace means excellent, great

indicators.note: sculpture means shaping, so these letters are remodelled

explanation.surface: Sculpture created in grand seats of learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sculpture' rearranges MADE to ADEM, put 'in' ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe is the academic world, the realm of universities and scholarship.

clue.text: Cool drink the setter had without flavour

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool
a sip is a small drink
the setter refers to themself as I; I had contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: The setter recalls a chilled drink that tasted of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Insipid food or drink is bland, lacking taste.

clue.text: Play area becoming small for tots

indicators.note: becoming means turning into, so one letter changes into another

parts.note: a drama is a play

explanation.surface: A play area turns into a small space for young children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tots' looks like toddlers; it means small measures of spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Drams and tots are both small measures of whisky or other spirits.

clue.text: Vehicle back ready for battle in part of ship

indicators.note: back means going backwards, so the cart's name is reversed

parts.note: a dray is a low cart, as used for carrying beer barrels
to arm is to make ready for battle

explanation.surface: A vehicle reverses, primed for combat aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses DRAY to YARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardarm is either end of a ship's yard, the spar holding a square sail.

clue.text: Only women answer about universal entities in philosophy

indicators.note: about means around, so the no-men phrase surrounds the letter

parts.note: a group of only women has no men
U is the film classification for universal

explanation.surface: A women-only reply on universal objects of philosophical study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Only women' is a whimsical way of describing a group with no men; 'about' wraps it round the universal letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Kant's philosophy, noumena are things in themselves, as opposed to phenomena perceived by the senses.

clue.text: Pass or cross through tip of Easter Island

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a cross is the letter X
Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: Travel past or across the end of Easter Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Easter Island' looks like one place; it splits into the tip of Easter and Crete.
explanation.definitionFit: To excrete is to discharge waste from the body, to pass it.

clue.text: Host's place, after dealing with criticism

indicators.note: after puts the vessel behind the word for concerning

parts.note: re means concerning, dealing with
a monstrance is the vessel in which the consecrated Host is displayed at Mass

explanation.surface: A host's home comes in for comment after a disagreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' is the communion bread, not someone entertaining guests.
explanation.definitionFit: A remonstrance is a forceful protest or complaint, a form of reproach.
